questions.statement: You are in the bathroom at night. You use water and soap to get clean. What do you do?
questions.context: Tomás vive en Pereira y antes de dormir se baña con agua tibia en el baño de su casa.

options.feedback: Correct. To take a shower means you wash your body with water and soap in the bathroom.
Incorrect. To have dinner means you eat the evening meal, and you do that at the table, not with soap.
Incorrect. To watch TV means you look at programs on a screen; it does not make you clean.
Incorrect. To do homework means you write and study school tasks, not wash your body.

questions.explanation: La expresión "take a shower" significa ducharse o bañarse con agua y jabón. Las otras opciones son rutinas reales, pero "have dinner" es comer, "watch TV" es ver televisión y "do homework" es hacer tareas.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Sofia eats rice and beans with her family at 7 p.m. What does she do at 7 p.m.?
questions.context: En Manizales, la familia de Sofia se sienta a comer arroz, frijoles y arepa a las 7 de la noche.

options.feedback: Correct. Dinner is the meal we eat in the evening, and 7 p.m. is in the evening.
Incorrect. Breakfast is the first meal of the day, in the morning, not at 7 p.m.
Incorrect. The text says she eats rice and beans; taking a shower is washing, not eating.
Incorrect. Children go to school in the morning, and the text talks about eating with her family.

questions.explanation: La cena se dice "dinner" y por eso decimos "She has dinner" cuando Sofia come por la noche. "Breakfast" es el desayuno de la mañana, así que no corresponde a las 7 p.m.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete: "Every evening, my brother ____ TV in the living room."
questions.context: Samuel vive en Barranquilla y todas las noches su hermano mayor ve televisión en la sala.

options.feedback: Incorrect. "My brother" is he, so the verb needs -s: watch is for I, you, we and they.
Incorrect. The -ing form needs "is" before it, and "every evening" asks for the present simple.
Incorrect. "To watch" is the infinitive; a sentence about a habit needs a conjugated verb.
Correct. With he or she the verb takes -es after "ch": he watches, so my brother watches.

questions.explanation: Cuando hablamos de una sola persona (he, she, my brother) el verbo en presente lleva -s o -es. Como "watch" termina en "ch", agregamos -es y queda "watches".
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement:
Teacher: "What do you do after school?"
Mateo: "____"
questions.context: En un colegio de Bucaramanga, la profesora pregunta a cada estudiante qué hace después de clases.

options.feedback: Incorrect. This answer tells his age, and the teacher asks about activities after school.
Incorrect. This answer tells the time, not an activity Mateo does.

options.text: I play soccer with my friends.
options.feedback: Correct. The question asks for an activity, and "I play soccer" names an activity Mateo does.
Incorrect. "Yes, I do" answers a yes/no question, but "What do you do" asks for information.

questions.explanation: La pregunta "What do you do after school?" significa qué haces después del colegio. Se responde con una actividad, como "I play soccer". Responder la edad o la hora no contesta lo que se pregunta.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement:
Read: "Laura gets home at 2 p.m. First, she has lunch. Then, she does her homework. At night, she reads a book and goes to bed."
What does Laura do right after lunch?
questions.context: Laura estudia en un colegio de Ibagué y llega a su casa a las 2 de la tarde.

options.feedback: Incorrect. She reads a book at night, which is later in the text, not right after lunch.
Correct. The word "Then" comes after lunch, and then she does her homework.
Incorrect. Going to bed is the last activity of the day in the text.
Incorrect. She gets home before lunch, at 2 p.m., so it is not after lunch.

questions.explanation: Las palabras "First" (primero) y "Then" (luego) muestran el orden. Primero Laura almuerza ("has lunch") y luego hace la tarea ("does her homework"). Leer y dormir ocurren en la noche.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.context: Juan José vive en Neiva; su papá se ducha cada noche antes de dormir porque hace mucho calor.

options.text: He take a shower at night.
options.feedback: Incorrect. With he the verb needs -s: "take" must change to "takes".

options.text: He taking a shower at night.
options.feedback: Incorrect. The -ing form needs "is" before it, and this is a habit, so it needs "takes".

options.text: He a shower takes at night.
options.feedback: Incorrect. The word order is wrong: in English the verb goes before "a shower".

options.text: He takes a shower at night.
options.feedback: Correct. He + takes is the present simple with -s, and the words are in the right order.

questions.explanation: En presente simple con he o she el verbo lleva -s: "He takes a shower". Además el orden es sujeto + verbo + complemento. Las otras oraciones olvidan la -s, usan -ing sin "is" o cambian el orden.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement:
Read: "Andres goes to bed at 8 p.m. He takes a shower before bed. He has dinner before his shower."
What is the correct order of his evening?
questions.context: Andres vive en Villavicencio y su mamá le pide seguir el mismo orden todas las noches.

options.feedback: Incorrect. The text says dinner is before his shower, so dinner must come first.
Incorrect. Going to bed is at the end, because the shower is before bed.
Correct. Dinner is before the shower, and the shower is before bed: dinner, shower, bed.
Incorrect. The shower is before bed, so bed cannot come before the shower.

questions.explanation: La palabra "before" significa antes. La cena va antes de la ducha y la ducha va antes de dormir, por eso el orden es: "dinner", "shower", "bed". Hay que leer cada pista y unirlas.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement:
Today is Monday. Camila says: "I watch TV after dinner, but on school nights I go to bed at 8:30." Her mom says: "Camila, it's 8:30!"
What should Camila do now?
questions.context: En Tunja, Camila tiene una regla en su casa para las noches de colegio.

options.feedback: Incorrect. She watches TV after dinner, but at 8:30 on a school night her rule says bed.
Correct. Monday is a school night and it is 8:30, the time Camila goes to bed.
Incorrect. TV comes after dinner, so dinner is already finished by 8:30.
Incorrect. Camila does not mention homework; her rule for 8:30 is to go to bed.

questions.explanation: Lunes es una noche de colegio ("school night"). Camila dice que esas noches se acuesta a las 8:30 ("go to bed"). Como su mamá dice que ya son las 8:30, lo correcto es irse a dormir.
questions.subject: ingles
